title: Federal statutory interpleader
summary: Statutory interpleader is a specific federal jurisdictional route for competing claims to money or property. The readings distinguish its minimal-diversity, fund, service, venue, and injunction provisions from ordinary Rule 22 interpleader.
notes: Do not import these special features into Rule 22, which requires its own ordinary subject-matter and personal-jurisdiction basis. The full text of § 1335 is in the Civil Procedure supplement on file (PDF page 150), linked below.

sections.Meaning: Statutory interpleader is a specific federal jurisdictional route for competing claims to money or property. The readings distinguish its minimal-diversity, fund, service, venue, and injunction provisions from ordinary Rule 22 interpleader.
sections.How to work through the question: Check the statutory amount, diversity among claimants, required deposit or bond, and the relevant service and venue provisions. Potential unliquidated claims can qualify under Tashire, but the scope of protective relief remains limited.
